records.quote: In a cyclic quadrilateral, each two opposite angles are supplementary.
records.claim: Theorem 3: In a cyclic quadrilateral, each two opposite angles are supplementary.

records.quote: Given: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.
records.text: Given: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. R.T.P: Prove that: (1) m(∠A) + m(∠C) = 180°; (2) m(∠B) + m(∠D) = 180°

records.quote: Proof:
records.caption: Circle with centre dot and inscribed quadrilateral ABCD (A top, B right, C bottom right, D left), used for the proof of Theorem 3.

records.quote: m (∠A) = 1/2 m (BCD)
records.text: Proof: since m(∠A) = 1/2 m(arc BCD), and m(∠C) = 1/2 m(arc BAD), therefore m(∠A) + m(∠C) = 1/2 [m(arc BCD) + m(arc BAD)] = 1/2 × 360° = 180°. Similarly: m(∠B) + m(∠D) = 180° (Q.E.D.)
records.notes: Proof steps recorded as one block; arcs written with arc symbol over BCD, BAD.

records.label: Example
records.quote: AB is a diameter in circle M, AC and AD are two chords
records.stem: In the opposite figure: $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter in circle M, $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{AD}$ are two chords in it and in one side from $\overline{AB}$. A tangent to the circle was drawn from B and intersected $\overrightarrow{AC}$ at X and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ at Y. Prove that: XYDC is a cyclic quadrilateral.
solution: ∴ $m(\angle ACB) = 90^\circ$ and $\angle ABC$ is complement to $\angle BAX$ (1)
∵ $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter and $\overrightarrow{BY}$ is tangent to the circle at B.
∴ $m(\angle ABX) = 90^\circ$ and $\angle AXB$ is complement to $\angle BAX$ (2)
∵ $\angle YDC$ is an exterior angle of the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD
∵ $\angle AXB$ is an exterior angle at the vertex of the quadrilateral XYDC and $\angle YDC$ is opposite to it.
records.notes: Solution steps 1 and 2 are marked with circled numbers 1 and 2 on the right.

records.quote: Y X B D C M A
records.caption: Circle with centre M and horizontal diameter AB (B at left, A at right). Chords AC and AD from A with C and D on the upper part of the circle. A tangent line at B is vertical, meeting ray AC at X and ray AD at Y (Y above X). Points in order up the tangent: B, X, Y. The small region XYDC is shaded yellow; a short dashed mark is on segment BC (drawn line BC). Labels: Y, D, X, C, B, M, A.
records.notes: Positions read from the figure; verify.

objectives.label: Use supplementary opposite angles
objectives.description: Find unknown angle and arc measures in a cyclic quadrilateral using the fact that opposite angles are supplementary (Theorem 3).

objectives.label: Use the exterior-angle corollary
objectives.description: Find an angle in a cyclic quadrilateral using the fact that an exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.

objectives.label: Prove a quadrilateral is cyclic from opposite angles
objectives.description: Decide that a quadrilateral is cyclic by showing two opposite angles are supplementary (converse of Theorem 3).

objectives.label: Prove a quadrilateral is cyclic from an exterior angle
objectives.description: Decide that a quadrilateral is cyclic by showing an exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.

objectives.label: Apply cyclic quadrilateral properties to solve problems
objectives.description: Combine the properties and their converses to prove results, identify cyclic quadrilaterals in a figure, and state the cases that make a quadrilateral cyclic.
